content.title: About
content.content: Fruit‑filled crepes are thin, delicate pancakes made from eggs, milk and flour, rolled around a sweet fruit filling that may include fresh or canned fruits, a touch of sugar and butter. They work well as a light breakfast, dessert or snack.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Crepes have ancient roots, with early versions known in Roman and Chinese cuisines.
Typical fruit fillings include apples, berries, peaches, pineapple, and even exotic mango.
In France, thin crepes are a classic dish often simply called “crêpes.”
The recipe can be adapted for dietary needs by using whole‑grain or gluten‑free flours.
Traditionally crepes are dusted with powdered sugar or drizzled with fruit sauce.

items.title: Rich in vitamins
items.content: Fruit fillings provide vitamin C, vitamin A and other antioxidants that support the immune system.

items.title: Source of fiber
items.content: Both the fruit and whole‑grain flour contribute dietary fiber, aiding digestion and satiety.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: When butter is used sparingly, crepes remain a light dish with modest saturated‑fat content.

items.title: Quick energy
items.content: Carbohydrates from the batter and fruit quickly replenish glycogen stores, useful before physical activity.

items.title: Heart‑friendly potassium
items.content: Fruits supply potassium, which helps maintain healthy blood pressure.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: Traditional flour contains gluten, which can trigger reactions in people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Fruit fillings are often sweetened, which may be a concern for individuals managing diabetes or sugar intake.

items.title: Additives in ready‑made fillings
items.content: Some pre‑made fruit mixes contain preservatives and artificial flavors.

items.title: Burn risk
items.content: Both batter and filling can be hot right after cooking; allow them to cool before serving.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve crepes warm, rolled or folded into triangles. They can be eaten by hand or with a fork. Enhance the filling with whipped cream, yogurt, honey, or a sprinkle of nuts.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep cooked crepes in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. Store the fruit filling separately to prevent the crepes from becoming soggy. For longer storage, freeze crepes in sealed bags at –18 °C and reheat in a microwave or skillet before serving.
